Priced stuff at weird amounts on purpose like $1.50 and $3.75 so she'd actually have to think about it instead of just doing round numbers. First hour she was slow and kept second-guessing herself, had a couple people wait a bit too long, but by the afternoon she was doing it fast in her head, even started counting back change out loud the old-school way (like "that's $6, that's $7...") which I didn't even teach her, she picked it up watching a video. Table was up about 4 hours total. She also had to track how much she started with vs ended with to make sure the math worked out at the end of the day.
rationale: Running a cash box with deliberately non-round prices and no calculator forced real-time subtraction and change-making under customer pressure, and reconciling the till at the end demonstrates basic bookkeeping accuracy applied to an actual small business transaction.
